hypothesis: In North Sea plaice sampled in late winter, the weight-length coefficient k = W/L^3 averaged by length class rises with length to a maximum near 30 cm, close to the length at which sexual maturity begins, and then declines slowly at larger sizes.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. Data: ICES DATRAS exchange-format CA (age/biology) records for the North Sea IBTS, quarter 1 (January-February, the closest survey season to Thompson's March 1907 sample), years 2015-2019, species Pleuronectes platessa (Aphia 127143), individual weight > 0, lengths converted to cm. Compute k = 1000 W/L^3 (W in g, L in cm) per fish, average by 1-cm length class over 15-50 cm keeping classes with >= 30 fish, smooth with a 3-class running mean, and let L* be the length of the maximum smoothed k. Maturity: from the same Q1 CA records with a maturity code, classify immature (scale code ending in 1) vs mature (codes ending 2-5), fit a logistic of maturity on length (sexes pooled; by sex reported) and take L50. Supports if all hold: (1) hump: L* is at least 3 cm above the smallest and 3 cm below the largest analysed class, and smoothed k(L*) exceeds smoothed k at both ends of the analysed range by >= 3%; (2) 25 <= L* <= 35 cm; (3) |L* - L50| <= 5 cm. Secondary (reported): the same by sex, and for quarter 3 (2017-2019).
fail_criterion: Refutes if smoothed k is flat (max - min over classes < 3% of the mean) or monotonic (maximum at an end of the analysed range), or if L* lies outside 22-38 cm. Mixed if a hump exists in the right place but is more than 5 cm from L50, or if the hump exists only in one sex or season.
interpretation: Thompson's k is the Fulton condition factor computed by length class from mean weights of trawl-caught plaice 'in a particular locality and at a particular time'. Modern survey fish are weighed individually, so class means of individual k are used, which is equivalent for the purpose. 'Near 30 cm' is read as 25-35 cm; 'about the size at which sexual maturity begins' is read as within 5 cm of the length at 50% maturity in the same samples, since the onset of maturity is not sharply defined. North Sea plaice today mature at smaller sizes than in 1907, so criterion (3) tests the coupling to maturity rather than the fixed 30 cm figure, while (2) tests the figure itself.

datasets.name: ICES DATRAS exchange data, CA records, North Sea IBTS quarter 1, 2015-2019
datasets.version: as served by getCAdata on the retrieval dates (DateofCalculation in records)
datasets.role: individual plaice length, weight, sex and maturity code (primary)

datasets.name: ICES DATRAS exchange data, CA records, North Sea IBTS quarter 3, 2017-2019
datasets.version: as served by getCAdata on the retrieval dates

method: Downloaded eight NS-IBTS CA XML files from the DATRAS web service, kept Pleuronectes platessa records (Aphia 127143; Q1 2015-2019: 12504 records, Q3 2017-2019: 9514), converted mm length classes to cm, and computed k = 10,000 W/L^3 per fish (11474 Q1 fish of 15-50 cm with weight). Class means of k by 1-cm length class (>= 30 fish) were smoothed with a 3-class running mean and the maximum located; the same was done by sex, by year and for Q3. Maturity codes were mapped to immature (…1) / mature (…2-5) and a maximum-likelihood logistic ogive gave L50 pooled and by sex (10464 Q1 fish with maturity codes).

measured.unit: cm, length class of maximum smoothed k in Q1 (upper end of analysed range 16-43 cm); k x 10^4 falls from 97.9 at 16 cm to a minimum of 93.1 at 26-27 cm and rises to 100.2 at 43 cm
measured.uncertainty: class means based on 36-646 fish per class; standard deviations in derived/k_by_length.csv; the same U-shape appears in each year, each sex and in Q3

caveats: The modern pattern is the inverse of Thompson's: k is highest in the smallest fish, falls to a minimum at 24-28 cm and rises again toward 40+ cm (a U, not a hump), in Q1 pooled, in each year 2015-2019, in each sex, and in Q3 (minimum 25-27 cm). No class near 30 cm is a maximum.

Scope difference: Thompson's 1907 fish came from 'a particular locality' in March with k from class mean weights; here fish are pooled across the whole North Sea survey and weighed individually. Spatial pooling can blur a local hump but cannot manufacture a minimum, and the by-year and by-sex replicates agree.

Maturity has shifted: North Sea plaice now reach 50% maturity at ~18 cm pooled (females 22.5 cm, males 15.2 cm) in Q1, far below the ~30 cm Thompson cited, so criterion (3) could not have been met at 30 cm even if a hump existed there. The k minimum (~26 cm) lies near the female L50, the opposite sign of the association Thompson proposed.
Notation: the pre-registration wrote k = 1000 W/L^3; the analysis reports k x 10^4 as Thompson did (plaice k ~ 100). The scaling does not affect any criterion.
Q3 maturity codes are sparse (1,652 fish) and Q3 L50 (~25 cm) differs from Q1; Q1 is the pre-registered primary season.
